query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled surface nitriding treatment on TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will increase its surface hardness and wear resistance while preserving the alloy’s beneficial bulk properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 alloy with relatively low hardness and poor friction/wear behavior.
generation.intervention: Apply a thermal nitriding process at a controlled temperature and duration to diffuse nitrogen into the surface, forming hard TiN/Ti2N compounds.
generation.conditions: Process temperatures around 900°C–1000°C for several hours under a nitrogen-rich atmosphere; testing under high-contact-stress and extreme-service conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a nanostructured nitride-enriched surface layer that does not alter the bulk α + β microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffusion leads to the formation of hard titanium nitride phases at the surface, thereby increasing hardness and improving wear resistance. The underlying material remains largely unaffected, preserving the alloy’s beneficial ductility and toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Treated TC4 will exhibit significantly increased surface hardness and reduced wear rates compared to untreated material, while maintaining its intrinsic ductility and fracture toughness.
generation.baseline: Properties of untreated α + β TC4 alloy.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness of the intervention is expected under the specific nitriding conditions (temperature, duration, and atmosphere) and may not translate if the processing parameters cause bulk phase alterations or thermal damage.
generation.uncertainty: Direct evidence linking thermal nitriding parameters to improved wear behavior on TC4 is lacking in the supplied records, and the optimum balance between enhanced surface properties and retention of bulk properties is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of TC4 subjected to the proposed nitriding process under controlled laboratory conditions alongside untreated controls. Measure surface hardness using microhardness testing (e.g., Vickers hardness test) and assess wear resistance through standardized pin-on-disk tests or similar high-contact-stress simulations.
measurements: Surface hardness values (e.g., Vickers hardness numbers) on treated vs untreated samples.
Wear track depth/volume loss measurements from pin-on-disk tests.
Visual and microscopic analysis of the treated layer to check for preservation of the bulk microstructure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided TC4 samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in surface hardness and reduction in wear rate compared to untreated samples, or if the treatment adversely affects the bulk mechanical properties (e.g., ductility or toughness), then the hypothesis is falsified.
